runs.query: Why can a goal call have valid evidence citations and still be false?

results.text:
In the final paid dribble check, both arms completed with **“Goal!” at source 6.0s**.
That establishes a feasible call under the supplied evidence timing; it omits the
dribble and shot sequence and supplies no analysis. It is a timing fix, not a
commentary-quality pass. No complete suite was rerun after these targeted changes.

## The important perception failure

The new cross/header observation invented a confirmed goal, complete with
`goal_line_crossing` and `ball_in_net` tags. Both writers followed that false
evidence. Structurally valid tags and citations therefore failed to protect
spoken factual accuracy.

Source frames at clip-relative 6, 7, 8 and 9 seconds show the goalkeeper continuing
play rather than a scored-goal outcome. The evaluator reference describes a headed
chance, not a goal. This was coding-agent source review, not human approval of the
reference or an independent blinded study.

A deliberate one-call check with the larger existing model used the identical
system prompt, source hash/window, sampler and output cap. **It also invented a
goal.** The check cost $0.016085 and did not justify changing production defaults.
The original baseline frame hashes were not independently saved; identical frame
bytes are inferred from the same source and sampler, rather than directly proven.

## Next work

Prioritize the observer's handling of this false goal using the existing bounded
inspection tools and explicit ball/goalmouth sequence evidence. Do not add a cue
tag in Python or feed the expected outcome to the observer to make the case pass.
Review the minimal necessary supporting frames too: unnecessarily late support
can leave a writer room for only one word even when an event was visible earlier.

Then resolve the three failed perception cases and repeat targeted text checks
under the corrected common contract. A controlled quality comparison needs usable
outputs, reviewed must-call meanings and consistent permissions before any
architecture or prompt-improvement claim. Keep all 15 development cases and every
failed attempt in the record; no broader dataset or new framework is needed.

# False-goal investigation — 9 November 2026

The confirmed failure is **overconfident visual classification followed by a
self-reported evidence check**. The observer invents a goal and the supporting
`ball_in_net` / `goal_line_crossing` tags together. The contract checks that these
fields are consistent; it does not independently verify the pixels. The caller
and joint writer then receive the same false confirmed event and narrate it.

This explains how the error reaches commentary. It does not fully explain the
model's internal visual mistake or establish a reliable runtime fix.

## Evidence before experiments

The original raw provider responses already contained the false goal, so Python
normalization, identity resolution and speaker phrasing did not create it.
Reconstructed JPEGs matched all ten saved larger-model input hashes exactly.
The underlying clip is 640×360 at approximately 29.97fps; the recorded observer
received one sampled frame per second. No stale input or source-window shift was
found. The disputed ball/goal configuration is small and visually ambiguous.

The relevant code path is `sample_clip` in `src/commentary/recorded_demo.py`,
`observe_recorded` in `src/commentary/replay/recorded.py`, and `supported_claim`
in `src/commentary/football.py`. The last function checks membership in a set
of cue names and requires support timestamps. It has no images to inspect.
This is a structural contract, not an independent visual verifier.

## Controlled checks

The [complete record](../examples/evaluation-results/false-goal-investigation-20261109.json)
contains source/frame hashes, actual prompt/block hashes, outputs, errors and
provider usage. The existing small model, output schema, output allowance and
reasoning setting stayed fixed. Each condition had two planned samples, with
no provider retries or schema-repair retries.

| Condition | Structurally accepted responses | Raw responses claiming a goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original framing, 1fps | 1/2 | 2/2 |
| Replace only “highlights” with “football” | 1/2 | 1/2 |
| Original framing, 2fps | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| Original framing plus goalmouth magnifications | 2/2 | 2/2 |

The two rejected responses still explicitly asserted a goal; their error was a
scene/action schema inconsistency. They must not count as correct abstentions.
The neutral-word response without a goal instead asserted a save; that alternative
was not independently verified and is not a recognition-quality pass.

The magnifications were manually specified diagnostic regions of frames 5, 6 and
7 seconds, taken from the old observer's claimed support times. Original full
frames remained available. No expected outcome, labels, transcript or previous
model claim was supplied. This tested attention to the disputed region, not an
autonomous crop-selection improvement. Upscaling adds no original source detail.

Neither denser sampling nor magnification removed this failure in these samples.
The wording result shows output sensitivity, but two samples cannot establish that
the word “highlights” is the cause. There is no supported one-parameter fix here.

## A more revealing inconsistency

A final neutral task asked the model only to locate the match ball in those same
three frames, without requesting an event or providing the earlier goal claim.
It marked the ball **ambiguous in all three frames**. Its coordinates were also
inconsistent with the earlier claim that the ball was clearly inside the left
side of the net. The localization output is another model prediction, not ground
truth or a trace of the model's internal reasoning.

This supports a diagnosis of poorly calibrated visual interpretation: event
narration commits to a familiar scoring story even when an object-level task
cannot establish clear ball positions. Raw responses then describe the keeper's
later recovery as happening “after the goal,” rather than reconsidering the
initial interpretation. Narrative completion is an inference from these outputs;
we cannot prove a particular internal neural mechanism.

## Fix direction and limits

Adding another cue tag or asking the same goal question again does not make the
evidence independent. A correction needs a more reliable ball/goal-plane check or
conservative abstention when that evidence cannot be established. It must also
retain real-goal detection: blocking every goal would game the test.

No runtime change was made or advertised as a fix in this investigation. A future
guard needs false-goal and real-goal controls before promotion. The diagnostic
harness is `scripts/investigate_false_goals.py`; its default is a free audit and
paid conditions require `--spend`. Regression tests use synthetic images only.

The investigation used nine call attempts, with a combined maximum budget of
$0.27. Reported token cost was **$0.0348588**, with no unsettled reservations.
No larger-model call, audio generation, new footage, training or deployment was
part of this investigation.

runs.query: Did saved lessons improve recognition on a different later penalty?

results.text:
# Learning from the last call

Public demo: https://www.aarshroongta.com/demo/noeri

**Latest finding:** the [later-incident transfer test](transfer/README.md) did
not establish improved recognition from memory. The current public view is an
illustration of saved lessons and later calls on a familiar incident, not proof
that lessons improve new events. No learning-success redesign was published.

The main UI now shows [a cumulative call history](session/README.md): multiple
earlier calls save lessons that later calls reference, over the same penalty
footage. The three-clip comparison below remains available as an earlier experiment.

One reviewed past failure becomes a model-written, persistent instruction for
three different clips. This is a small application-level memory experiment using
existing models, inspired by Noeri's work on agents that improve from experience.
No Noeri API, weight updates, fine-tuning, RL, search, fresh vision, or TTS ran.

## Source and protocol

The lesson comes from the rejected England–France analyst call in
`examples/evaluation-results/researched-handoff-20261107.json`. The analyst
claimed a keeper touch from a weak audit tag. A retained coding-agent correction
identifies that unsupported detail. This is not independent human feedback.

GPT-5.4 Mini distilled `lesson.json` from that failure and correction. It contains
no match names or transfer answers. The file was saved before transfer calls.
The same lesson, unchanged after the initial pilot, was used for all later calls.

The three transfer cases were preselected as `goal`, `dribble`, and `save`, from
the existing 15-clip development suite. They use different source files from the
lesson source. The writer receives only their saved observations; reference
labels, expected commentary, research and earlier calls are excluded. These are
full-context offline text reactions, not causal live playback or a vision test.

The comparison uses a compact experimental writer, not the current production
role prompts. The same model, base instructions, evidence, output schema, and
output allowance are used in both arms. Only the memory instructions differ.
There is one sample per arm, counterbalanced call order, and no automatic retries.
Every planned case and output is retained, including the regression.

## Results

| Case | Without memory | With memory | Review |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Save | Adds “at the near post,” absent from the supplied observations; 38 words | Retains the save, removes the unsupported location, qualifies the follow-up; 31 words | Favorable single example |
| Crowded goalmouth | Narrates uncertain delivery/contact as established; 32 words | Qualifies the final touch, but still cites uncertainty and exceeds the word target; 37 words | Mixed |
| Dribble and finish | Compact supported outcome; 23 words | Adds unnecessary uncertainty and repetitive analysis; 50 words | Regression |

Review was performed by a coding agent against the supplied observations, not
independent pixels. Saved perception can itself be false. Existing citation IDs
are not proof of factual support. The save example is not a repeatable accuracy

# A growing memory across calls

Public replay: https://www.aarshroongta.com/demo/noeri

The UI shows three exact bad calls, each directly paired with its saved lesson,
and three later calls or decisions. Everything is visible immediately; a single
penalty video is independently playable. Later calls received cumulative memory
plus their own preceding dialogue. Green highlights show the lesson IDs returned
by the model.
This replaces the clip comparison as the main experience; the earlier three-clip
experiment, including its regression, is retained in the parent directory.

## What is real

- Earlier calls are exact retained lines from three takes of the England–France
  penalty in `examples/evaluation-results/researched-handoff-20261107.json`.
- The contact and score corrections come from that retained investigation.
  The repetition correction is a new coding-agent editorial review, not human
  feedback. The three takes are arranged in review order, not original run order.
- A model distilled each correction separately, then the script persisted the
  growing list after each lesson. The three principles are unedited model output.
- Three new calls actually received all three saved lessons, the same saved
  observations and preceding new dialogue. The final call chose to abstain.
- Raw outputs, exact prompts/inputs, source hashes and costs are retained here.
  Model-selected lesson references are inspectable but not proof that a lesson
  caused a particular phrase. All three lessons were supplied; this is not a
  retrieval-system benchmark. The score lesson was not referenced by the model.

This is a reconstructed review history and a later pass over a **familiar event**.
It demonstrates memory persistence and reuse, not generalization to new events,
autonomous discovery of errors, live model timing, or flawless improvement. The
later analyst still partly repeats the goal. No new visual recognition ran.

An input-recording bug kept a shared dialogue list, so later dialogue appeared
in earlier records when the final report was serialized. The actual requests
had already been serialized before later calls existed. The saved inputs were
restored from the preceding outputs and verified against their original pre-call
hashes. `original-capture.json` preserves the uncorrected record, and the recorder
now snapshots the list. No model calls or generated words were replaced.

The single source window gives visual context for all the earlier takes and
later calls. There is no staged walkthrough or playback gate. This is not one
causal run through a match, and video timing does not represent API timings.
No speech was synthesized. The seven-second source window starts at 50.5 seconds
in `clips/action-sources/england-france-penalties.mp4`. The source-file hash is in
`session.json`. The footage is muted and has no added commentary captions.

## Cost and checks

Six GPT-5.4 Mini calls: three lesson extractions and three subsequent role calls.
Reported token cost: **$0.00531675**, under a $0.10 hard cap, with no unsettled
reservations. No retries, larger models, search, fresh vision, TTS, training, RL,

claim; the broad lesson also causes harm. Two memory scripts meet the 35-word
target; one does not. Words are counted with Python `str.split()`, including any
inline citation strings actually emitted by the model. Text is not rewritten.

The first pilot reused a legacy long-script prompt with conflicting short-output
instructions. Three of six writer responses failed parsing. `pilot.json` and
`pilot-responses/` retain that attempt. After fixing the base prompt for both
arms, the comparison reused the original lesson and made six fresh writer calls.
This was a protocol correction, not a reroll of one unfavorable arm.

Total reported model token cost: **$0.01583775 across 13 calls**, including lesson
extraction and the failed pilot. The pilot's $0.01025775 settled spend plus the
second run's $0.18 hard cap remained below the overall $0.20 ceiling. No unsettled
reservations remain. All calls used GPT-5.4 Mini, reasoning none, no retries,
with at most 400 lesson tokens or 600 writer output tokens.

## Reproduce

Free audit:

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/lesson_experiment.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_lesson_memory.py -q
```

A new paid comparison with the frozen lesson (use a new output directory):

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/lesson_experiment.py --spend --max-usd 0.10 \
  --lesson "$PWD/examples/lesson-memory/lesson.json" \
  --out runs/lesson-memory/new-comparison
```

Omit `--lesson` to distill a fresh lesson first. New results require review; the
script never overwrites or automatically promotes them to the published demo.
`result.json` contains the reviewed comparison, source/input/prompt/lesson hashes,
actual outputs, and usage. `response-*.json` retains the six raw provider results.

## Website

The canonical buildless UI lives in `web/public/learning-calls/`. Mirror that
directory into `../personal-website/public/learning-calls/`; `/demo/noeri` is a
Vercel rewrite. The static page shows saved results without API calls. Its
main view shows the earlier mistake, the exact saved lesson, and the next caller
line with and without it. Full caller/analyst outputs and the other two cases
are under one disclosure. The experiment persisted the lesson to disk and
actually supplied it to the model before generating calls.

The cumulative replay adds a muted window of the existing penalty footage.
All generated words, the full lesson, and the failed pilot remain inspectable.
No outreach message has been sent.

runs.query: Why was the optional reviewer turned off for the penalty commentary?

results.text:
# Selected automatic portfolio demo

`penalty-plan.json` contains exact generated words and source cues for the
20-second England–France sequence. `penalty-trace.json` retains source metadata,
research, identity lookup decisions, role actions, rejected turns and budget.
The web summary is `web/data/portfolio-demo.json`.

`selection.json` preserves both bounded attempts and the choice of attempt two.
The first optional reviewer rejected a valid short goal call; the second attempt
ran without that reviewer. An early oversized line was rejected in the second
attempt, leaving a caller penalty/run-up/goal sequence and an analyst response.
No model-written words were manually edited. These are selected development
outputs on reused perception, not an automatic baseline quality benchmark.

Saved vision came from the prior continuity candidate, with its script excluded
from runtime input. The original full-context vision preparation saw a longer
window; only saved observations inside the selected 20 seconds are used here. Resolved names were cleared and re-proposed using the saved,
cited England squad. No new vision, research or voice generation was performed.
Total reported token cost for both attempts: $0.02666745, under a $0.24 cap.

Render a silent captioned clip with scripts/render_text_demo.py. Local MP4s are
ignored; plans, transcripts, traces and render tooling are retained. See
[the portfolio guide](../../docs/PORTFOLIO.md) and
[the case study](../../docs/PORTFOLIO_CASE_STUDY.md).

## Matched before/after iteration

`before-plan.json` and `before-trace.json` retain attempt one. `iteration.json`
records matched-input hashes, the reviewer intervention, observed role/cost changes
and limitations. The local player can switch both source-timed captioned versions.
This is a focused development case following the 15-clip pilot, not the earliest
system baseline or a claim that every output dimension improved. No additional
model calls were made to package the comparison.

## Fresh vision and light edits

The additional featured clips are in [release](release/README.md), with fresh
perception, raw outputs, every attempted run, exact edit records and no added
football facts. These replace the heavily rewritten showcases in the player.

# Text evaluation trial — 9 November 2026

The pilot found execution and perception failures. **It does not demonstrate that
the multi-agent writer improves commentary.** No candidate was promoted.

The [saved record](../examples/evaluation-results/text-comparison-20261109.json)
contains per-case outputs, rejected drafts, errors, hashes, call summaries, budgets
and limited agent review. The combined experiment had a maximum budget of **$1**.
Reported token cost was **$0.17030795**, with no unsettled reservations: 77 call
attempts using `gpt-5.4-mini` and one deliberate perception-only check using
`gpt-5.4-2026-03-05`. No TTS, fresh research, training or deployment occurred.
Regression tests used scripted backends.

## Completion is different from quality

The suite pilot used identical saved perception within each pair, a $0.02 cap per
writer arm, reasoning effort `none`, 1,024 output tokens per call, zero provider
retries, and at most one validation repair. The optional agent reviewer was off.
Perception preparation had a separate shared $0.24/eight-call cap. It reused seven
historical bundles and attempted the other eight once each.

| Stage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Perception inputs | 12/15 usable: seven reused, five generated. |
| Perception failures | Corner: inconsistent goal/scene output; foul-decision: invalid frame timestamps; offside: confirmed action without required supporting cue. |
| Writer execution | 5/24 attempted arms completed structural validation; 19 failed. Six additional arms were missing because their perception failed. |
| Complete pairs | Cross/header and penalty. Card had one complete arm. |
| Source review | Both cross/header candidates falsely announce a goal. The penalty candidates correctly call the named low finish; this is one short development example. |
| Whole-suite acceptance | None. References remain unreviewed and major failures remain. |

The original suite pilot, `short-clips-v2`, also exposed a validation asymmetry:
the role loop rejected caller references to uncertain/replay actions, whereas the
joint adapter did not apply that same gate. This was corrected in v3. **Do not use
the v2 completion counts to rank architectures.** They are integration diagnostics.
All original results remain recorded rather than replaced with later successes.

## What changed after the failures

The first $0.0083 penalty smoke showed that the historical writer's long-clip turn
quotas conflicted with short windows. The adapter removed those quotas and supplied
explicit timing information. The subsequent suite still exposed drafts that could
not fit after their latest supporting frame. Repair feedback that merely said a
line ended too late was ineffective.

Targeted development checks on dribble and goal then added per-evidence remaining
word allowances. The final `short-clips-v4` adapter reports the exact number of
words that fit in validation feedback, applies the same uncertainty/replay gate
to both writers, and stops asking the caller again after an analyst abstention
when no newer eligible evidence exists. The original demo/live paths are unchanged.

or Noeri API calls were used. Including the earlier experiment, this session's
total reported model-token spend is $0.0211545.

Free audit and regression checks:

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/memory_session.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_memory_session.py tests/test_lesson_memory.py -q
```

To regenerate, choose a new output directory and explicitly enable spending:

```sh
.venv/bin/python scripts/memory_session.py --spend --out runs/lesson-memory/new-session
```

New output needs review before publication. Nothing automatically overwrites the
saved demonstration. Each call input receives observations, not reference labels
or expected commentary. Corrections are supplied only in lesson extraction.

Render the footage locally without model calls:

```sh
ffmpeg -ss 50.5 -i clips/action-sources/england-france-penalties.mp4 \
  -t 7 -an -vf 'scale=640:-2' -c:v libx264 -preset fast -crf 23 \
  -movflags +faststart web/public/learning-calls/penalty.mp4
```

The commentary repo ignores video assets. The public portfolio serves this small
derived clip alongside the buildless UI. No outreach has been sent.
